prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1412; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a left-turn collision at an intersection and stated a knee injury from the impact. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and has provided a consistent account on each contact so far.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and spoke with two witnesses, who both confirm the collision occurred as described and that the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. The other driver's statement matches in full.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene and the repair estimate show front-end damage consistent with the described impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is on file, and nothing indicates the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy. Requested prior medical records for the knee and found no earlier injury to that body area on record.

Entry 5: Medical file shows the knee injury is consistent with the force and direction of a side impact of this kind. Treatment followed a typical course, with therapy visits gradually reducing as the claimant improved.

Entry 6: Claimant continues to report steady recovery and has given the same account of the accident in every conversation. Based on the evidence gathered, the claim is moving forward for standard processing.
